decision_rule: For k in {8,16,32}, best-of-first-k-seeds per method (paired seeds); gap(k) = rigid_best(k) - harden_best(k) at tolerance 1e-4. PRIMARY: gap(32) > gap(8) + 1e-4 on >=5/6 instances -> one-sided sign test, alpha 0.05 -> hardening's advantage widens with seed budget (rare-basin discovery). If gap is flat, the advantage is a fixed offset, not a discovery effect. Report full discovery curves (best vs seeds) per instance and method.
hypothesis: Hardening's advantage is a rare-basin discovery effect: rigid's best plateaus early (it cannot find the basin at any budget) while harden keeps discovering better basins as seeds grow. Motivated by the squ n=11 duplicate: 16 seeds missed the signature (Y=0), 32 seeds found it (Y=1).
question: Does hardening's advantage grow with seed budget (rare-basin discovery)?
title: Seed scaling: discovery curves on signature instances
